english.title: Sell / supply for slaughter for human consumption animal which contains unauthorised substance / product

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Examination for Residues and Maximum Residue Limits

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[sold]_
(B)_[supplied]_

for slaughter for human consumption an animal, namely **(..SPECIFY ANIMAL..),

(C)_[which contained or to which there had been administered an unauthorised substance,]_
(D)_[to which there had been administered a substance in contravention of regulation 5 of the Animals and Animal Products (Examination for Residues and Maximum Residue Limits) Regulations 1997,]_
(E)_[which was an aquaculture animal to which a substance listed in Annex II or III of Council Directive 96/23/EC(2) had been administered,]_
(F)_[to which a list A substance or a substance listed in Annex III of Council Directive 96/23/EC(2) had been administered,]_
(G)_[which contained a Table 1 substance at a concentration exceeding the maximum residue limit,]_
(H)_[to which a medicinal product had been administered and the withdrawal period for that product had not expired,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY SUBSTANCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 9 and 23 of the Animals and Animal Products (Examination for Residues and Maximum Residue Limits) Regulations 1997.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time Limit on Prosecutions
No prosecution shall be begun after the expiry of -

(a) three years from commission of the offence; or
(b) one year from its discovery by the prosecutor,

whichever is the earlier.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
